title: Full Stack Engineer
description:
The opportunity

We're looking for a mid-level to senior Full Stack Engineer to build the software that powers materials discovery, from the interfaces scientists use down to the services and data models behind them.

Reporting to the Director of Digital Experience and work closely with the rest of the software engineering team, most of your time will be spent on the frontend: crafting the interfaces scientists and engineers use to navigate vast datasets, turn dense experimental results into charts and interactive graphics they can actually reason about, interact wi
evaluation_framework:
### Frontend Development (TypeScript, HTML, CSS) 
Classification: CORE_MANDATORY 
Evaluation Criteria: Minimum 4 years of professional experience with TypeScript, HTML, and CSS (Tailwind preferred). Ability to build responsive, mobile-first interfaces. 
Scoring Guidance: 1-2: Less than 4 years experience. 5-6: 4 years experience with basic proficiency. 7-8: Strong experience with complex, responsive layouts. 9-10: Expert-level mastery of modern CSS/TS and architectural patterns. 

### Frontend Frameworks (Svelte/SvelteKit) 
Classification: CORE_MANDATORY 
Evaluation Criteria: Proficiency in Svelte/SvelteKit or strong experience in React/Vue with a demonstrated willingness to learn Svelte. 
Scoring Guidance: 1-2: No experience with modern component-based frameworks. 5-6: Strong React/Vue experience but no Svelte. 7-8: Proficient in Svelte/SvelteKit. 9-10: Deep expertise in Svelte/SvelteKit, including state management and reactivity. 

### Backend Development (Go) 
Classification: CORE_MANDATORY 
Evaluation Criteria: Professional experience with a statically typed, compiled language (Go preferred; Java, C#, Rust, or C++ acceptable). 
Scoring Guidance: 1-2: No experience with compiled, statically typed languages. 5-6: Experience in a similar language (e.g., Java/C#). 7-8: Strong Go experience. 9-10: Expert in Go and building performant backend services. 

### API Design and Data Contracts 
Classification: CORE_MANDATORY 
Evaluation Criteria: Experience designing and evolving API contracts, specifically gRPC and Protocol Buffers. 
Scoring Guidance: 1-2: No experience with API contracts. 5-6: Experience with REST/GraphQL. 7-8: Strong experience with gRPC/Protobuf. 9-10: Expert in managing schema evolution and backward compatibility. 

### Database Management (MongoDB) 
Classification: IMPORTANT 
Evaluation Criteria: Working knowledge of document stores (MongoDB preferred), including schema design, indexing, and migrations. 
Scoring Guidance: 3-4: Basic CRUD knowledge. 5-6: Experience with document stores. 7-8: Strong experience with MongoDB indexing and production migrations. 9-10: Expert in data modeling and performance optimization for document databases. 

### Data Visualization 
Classification: IMPORTANT 
Evaluation Criteria: Hands-on experience building data visualizations for scientific or complex datasets (D3, SVG, Canvas). 
Scoring Guidance: 3-4: Basic charting library usage. 5-6: Experience with D3 or similar. 7-8: Strong ability to build custom, performant visualizations. 9-10: Expert in high-performance, custom scientific data visualization. 

### Full Stack Ownership 
Classification: IMPORTANT 
Evaluation Criteria: Ability to own features end-to-end, from data model to UI, without relying on backend/frontend silos. 
Scoring Guidance: 3-4: Prefers working in one layer. 5-6: Comfortable crossing boundaries occasionally. 7-8: Proven track record of full-stack feature delivery. 9-10: Exceptional ability to architect and ship across the entire stack independently. 

### AI and Agentic Systems 
Classification: NICE_TO_HAVE 
Evaluation Criteria: Familiarity with agentic systems, tool calls, MCP, or AI-frontend integration (e.g., Vercel AI SDK). 
Scoring Guidance: 3: No experience but interest. 5-6: Basic exposure to AI SDKs or LLM integration. 7-8: Practical experience building AI-integrated features. 9-10: Deep expertise in agentic workflows and AI-driven UI.

title: ML Research Engineer
description:
The Role

Our scientific agent decides what experiment to run next. This role builds the machinery that lets us understand, evaluate, and continuously improve the agent's decisions.

You will work closely with the Principal Scientist to turn hypotheses about agent behavior into reproducible experiments and production improvements. Your initial focus will be evaluation datasets, replay, trajectory analysis, and the policies governing how the agent plans, responds to results, and recovers from failure.

evaluation_framework:
### Production ML Systems Experience
Classification: CORE_MANDATORY
Evaluation Criteria: 4-8 years of experience building production ML systems, research infrastructure, or data-intensive backends.
Scoring Guidance: 1-2: Less than 4 years or no production ML experience. 5-7: 4-6 years of relevant experience. 8-10: 7+ years with a proven track record of shipping end-to-end ML systems.

### Python and Software Engineering Discipline
Classification: CORE_MANDATORY
Evaluation Criteria: Proficiency in Python, testing, typing, packaging, and CI/CD practices.
Scoring Guidance: 1-2: Lacks software engineering rigor. 5-7: Competent in Python with standard testing/CI practices. 9-10: Expert-level Python with deep experience in production-grade software engineering.

### ML Evaluation and Experimentation
Classification: CORE_MANDATORY
Evaluation Criteria: Experience with offline evaluation harnesses, dataset/split design, metric design, and statistical reasoning.
Scoring Guidance: 1-2: No experience with ML evaluation. 5-7: Familiar with basic evaluation metrics. 9-10: Deep expertise in designing robust, reproducible evaluation frameworks for complex ML systems.

### Data Pipeline and Infrastructure Skills
Classification: IMPORTANT
Evaluation Criteria: Experience with schema design, versioning, and orchestration tools (e.g., Airflow, Prefect, Dagster, Ray).
Scoring Guidance: 3-4: Basic data handling. 5-6: Experience with at least one orchestration tool. 9-10: Expert in designing scalable data pipelines and infrastructure.

### Reproducibility and Scientific Rigor
Classification: IMPORTANT
Evaluation Criteria: Ability to conduct controlled experiments, manage pinned environments, and ensure results are reproducible.
Scoring Guidance: 3-4: Basic understanding of versioning. 7-8: Strong track record of reproducible research. 9-10: Exceptional ability to turn ambiguous problems into controlled, scientific experiments.

### LLM Agents and Sequential Decision Making
Classification: NICE_TO_HAVE
Evaluation Criteria: Experience with LLM agents (tool calling, planning loops) or sequential decision making (RL, bandits, Bayesian optimization).
Scoring Guidance: 3: No experience. 5-6: Familiarity with LLM agent concepts. 7-8: Practical experience building or evaluating agents. 9-10: Deep expertise in agentic workflows or RL.

### Observability and Experiment Tracking
Classification: NICE_TO_HAVE
Evaluation Criteria: Experience with tools like Langfuse, MLflow, Weights and Biases, DVC, or observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana).
Scoring Guidance: 3: No experience. 5-6: Used one or more tools. 7-8: Advanced usage of experiment tracking and observability in production.

### Domain Expertise (Scientific/Lab Automation)
Classification: NICE_TO_HAVE
Evaluation Criteria: Background in scientific computing, materials/chemistry data, lab automation, or robotics.
Scoring Guidance: 3: No experience. 5-6: Relevant academic or tangential industry experience. 7-10: Direct experience in self-driving labs or high-throughput scientific automation.
